coverage.reason: Preserve the correct source region for distant attacks after the current Core map-definition cache evicts opaque city IDs. The shared ID lookup falls back to retained city state; submitted army endpoints and route membership retain explicit mission regions. The new browser regression uses actual Core IDs and the current 81-map topology, evicts the source definition, verifies server-preview gating and error retry, submits the attack, and checks retained order endpoints after the source leaves visible state at desktop and two landscape-mobile sizes. Main-city recovery and report navigation fixtures now provide the runtime city lookup and protect callers of the changed shared helper. Owned-city cross-map synchronization and pending-departure tests cover roster retention, ownership loss, order reconciliation and recovery. World-travel tests protect reciprocal roads, cold/evicted caches, disconnected routes, terrain distance, long-route persistence and authoritative preview matching. The world-travel emulator suite checks authoritative preview/launch endpoint validation and forged-route rejection for the affected client payload boundary. No server implementation, topology, balance or production data is changed; build and asset validation run through prepare-pr.
